requirement: The bundled skills MUST tell agents that sites need no reference to the requirement, that `habeas author --all` authors site reviews under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and that a false site review is addressed by fixing the site, or by tightening the queries or the requirement text when the site should not be covered or the text admits more than one reading, under {cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`, not by re-running the review.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.reviews` states only what the bundled skills must say to agents. Those are three points: sites need no reference to the requirement; `habeas author --all` authors site reviews, citing `requirements.references.site_review`; and a false site review is fixed by changing the site, the queries or the requirement text, citing `requirements.cli.flip_guidance`, not by re-running the review. The clause "The bundled skills MUST tell agents…" constrains content that agents can read. It does not name a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. Take any alternative that puts the same guidance in different words, in a different section, or in a different bundled skill file. It would still satisfy the text, so where and how the guidance is written is discretionary. The two review roots are `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md` and `assets/skills/habeas-evidence/references/reviews.md`. They are documentation files whose outline is only a section node. They are the places where that observable content could appear, and they do not form a structural implementation. The cited declarations `requirements.references.site_review` and `requirements.cli.flip_guidance` supply context only. Whether the guidance is actually present and correct is a behavioral, content-level question. It is not a structural one, so no {impl} reference is needed here.

behavioral: The subject is `requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.reviews`. Its only test is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_explain_site_references_and_site_reviews]`, which is marked `{test}`. Its helpers `section`, `assert_text`, `assert_text_in_order`, `skill_file` and `distributed_reference` really do assert that the phrases are present. `assert_text` panics if a phrase is missing, and `assert_text_in_order` also enforces the order.

The obligations and the assertions that cover them:
- **Sites need no reference.** The `## Don't` section of the habeas skill's `references/distributed-requirements.md` must contain "Don't reference the distributed requirement from a site just because it is a site; sites need none."
- **`habeas author --all` authors site reviews.** The `## Do` section must contain "Let `habeas author --all` author the site reviews." The `## Review` section must contain "`habeas author --all` authors a site review for each site". The habeas-evidence `references/reviews.md`, section `## Site reviews`, must contain "authored by `habeas author --all`".
- **A false site review is fixed at the site.** `reviews.md` must contain "1. If it does apply, fix the code at the site."
- **Tighten the queries or text.** `reviews.md` must then contain "2. If the site should not be covered, narrow the site query or tighten the text describing sites; if the obligation's text admits a reading under which the site fails, tighten that text". These phrases are checked in order, and the hand-off "take them through habeas-requirements steps 3 to 5" must follow them. The `## Don't` section must also contain "fix the site, or tighten the queries or the text". Together these cover both alternatives the requirement names: the site should not be covered, and the text admits another reading.
- **Not by re-running the review.** The `## Don't` section must contain "Don't re-run a false site review for a different result; ...".

I treated "under {cite}" as context. The obligations of `requirements.references.site_review` and `requirements.cli.flip_guidance` are assessed elsewhere and need no test here.

The skill wording for the second alternative is "admits a reading under which the site fails", while the requirement says "admits more than one reading". I judged these close enough that a careful reviewer would not call it a gap.

I found no untested obligation, no wrong expectation and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} distributed_guidance.reviews

The bundled skills MUST tell agents that sites need no reference to the requirement, that `habeas author --all` authors site reviews under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and that a false site review is addressed by fixing the site, or by tightening the queries or the requirement text when the site should not be covered or the text admits more than one reading, under {cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`, not by re-running the review.
:::{req} site_review
Every site of a distributed requirement under
{cite}`requirements.references.distributed` MUST have a site review: an
assessment of whether that site upholds the requirement, recorded at
`evidence/sites/<full-name>/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` and
`<selector>` are encoded as under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. The review MUST use the prompt
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.site_prompt`. Mandatory inputs, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the site's outline
node, the requirement's complete declaration, and each declaration the
requirement cites. The record MUST contain the requirement's full name, the
site's file and selector, `queries`, the sorted names of the queries with a
match at the site, `applies`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`, with
determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. `applies` MUST be a
Boolean recording whether the requirement applies to the site. A site to which
the requirement does not apply MUST be judged `true`, and the rationale MUST
explain why it does not apply. `habeas info` MUST report, for each selected
distributed requirement, how many of its sites the requirement does not apply
to.
Validation MUST require a current, accepted review for every site, MUST report a
false review with its rationale, and MUST report stale, missing, or orphaned
reviews; a review is orphaned when its file and selector no longer name a site
of the requirement. A `{fixme}` naming the requirement inside a site
acknowledges a gap at that site only: it MUST be an input to that site's review
and MUST NOT contribute to the requirement's own review, coverage, or reference
set. A review MUST become stale when the site's hash, the requirement's
declaration, a cited declaration, its `queries`, or the `{fixme}` references
naming the requirement inside the site, with the words of their bodies, change.
Each site review's determination MUST be checked on its own, independently of
the requirement's evidence. Authoring with `--all` MUST include site reviews,
`habeas author sites:<full-name>` MUST author the site reviews of the named
requirement, and `habeas author sites:<full-name>/<file>#<selector>` MUST author
the review of the one site it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>` names the
file's root node. `habeas status` MUST report missing, stale, invalid, and false
site reviews with their requirement, file, and selector, and `habeas info` MUST
list each selected requirement's sites with their determinations.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
:::{req} flip_guidance
The `habeas-evidence` skill MUST state the goal that independent assessments
of the same subject reach the same determination, because the requirement, code,
and tests leave no gap a careful reviewer could find and no reading a careful
reviewer could take differently, and the other bundled skills MUST refer to it
rather than restate it. The skills MUST tell agents that assessments of the
same subject that disagree are findings against that goal. They MUST direct agents to read both
rationales and decide whether one assessment found a real gap or the requirement
text admits more than one reading, then fix the source or tests, or tighten the
requirement text, rather than re-running an assessment to obtain a different
determination. Every change to agreed requirement text, including a rewording for precision,
MUST be reviewed with the user under
{cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.agreed_text` before it is committed, and the
skills MUST then direct agents to give the reason, and the rationale that
prompted the change, in the message of the commit that makes it. That message
MUST describe the change relative to the prior commit, not the intermediate
drafts that led to it.
